newsitem.title: USA: SEC's Levitt to meet muni groups on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: SEC's Levitt to meet muni groups on yield burning.

text.p: SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt has agreed to meet with seven municipal groups on their request that a presidential panel assume decisionmaking over the volatile "yield burning" issue, a National League of Cities official said on Wednesday.

The League, National Governors' Association, National Conference of State Legislatures, U.S. Conference of Mayors, National Association of Counties, and two other groups requested the meeting in a March 18 letter to Levitt, said the League official, Frank Shafroth, director of policy and federal relations.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance their outstanding bonds.
The Internal Revenue Service has told municipalities that they can avoid having bonds declared taxable by settling any overcharges with the agency.

But muni groups told top Treasury brass at a Jan 27 closed meeting that bond dealers, not issuers, in general should pay the overcharges, following aggressive enforcement action by the SEC. Treasury officials have not responded.

Groups wrote to Levitt on March 18 because he is part of the President's Working Group on Financial Markets. Chaired by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, the group includes the heads of the Federal Reserve Board, SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
It was formed by a presidential executive order March 1.
The groups want the working group brought in to oversee decisionmaking on the yield burning issue, group members said.
Muni groups also have requested a meeting with Marcia Hale, a special assistant to Clinton, on the issue. A spokesman for the groups said Hale has not yet agreed to a meeting.
